content: Young individuals are increasingly taking on roles as entrepreneurs and innovators, particularly in fields such as education, science, and technology. They are leveraging their skills and expanding their efforts to drive climate action forward. To create health-promoting environments for children and adolescents, several strategies can be implemented: 1. Addressing the Impact of E-Waste on Children and Adolescents: Eliminate child labor in e-waste processing and integrate adult and youth workers into the formal economy with fair working conditions across the entire value chain, including collection, processing, recycling, and resale. Advocate for responsible e-waste recycling by engaging policymakers, communities, waste workers, and their families. Conduct further research and collect data on the involvement of women, children, and adolescents in e-waste processing. Raise awareness about the health risks associated with e-waste recycling, particularly for women and children. 2. Preparing Schools for Future Pandemics and Ensuring Inclusive WASH (Water, Sanitation, and Hygiene) Services: Build or upgrade educational facilities to be child-, disability-, and gender-sensitive. Provide safe and effective learning environments equipped with access to safe drinking water, sanitation, and hygiene services. 3. Promote the universal use of clean technologies and fuels for household cooking, heating, and lighting, ensuring affordability and accessibility for low-income families through social support mechanisms. Implement better waste management practices to reduce the burning of waste in communities, thereby decreasing air pollution. Investigate the health risks posed by emerging chemicals, such as endocrine-disrupting substances, to adolescents and across the life course. 4. Encouraging and Supporting Climate Action by and for Adolescents and Children: Develop engaging, age-appropriate multimedia content and interactive tools to educate and inspire youth-led climate action. Promote social and behavioral change through sustainable education, youth-led environmental initiatives, outreach campaigns, and public engagement activities that address the indirect drivers of biodiversity loss and environmental degradation. Enforce eco-labeling and standard-setting schemes to inform consumers about the environmental impact of products and enhance adolescents' understanding of eco-labeling. Strengthen environmental digital literacy and e-governance skills among youth to enable their active participation in addressing the environmental aspects of digital transformation. Amplify youth activism and voices to garner support for positive environmental changes, reduce pollution, and promote sustainable, healthier living. Collaborate with health and education ministries to encourage and support sustainable lifestyle changes that reduce greenhouse gas emissions. This includes collecting disaggregated data by age and sex, focusing on the unique needs of adolescents, and involving them in participatory research and evaluation processes. Global frameworks, such as the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and the Global Strategy for Women’s, Children’s, and Adolescents’ Health, emphasize the importance of addressing adolescent health as a critical component of achieving broader health and development goals.
